observations.code_quote: "description": "Per-owning-team rollup of the CI test surfaces each team owns, over a window (date_from default -14d, maximum 30 days). It reads the same per-run evidence as engineering-analytics-flaky-tests and means the same thing by flaky: flaky_test_count is owned tests one commit was seen both failing and passing in the window (a re-run attempt went green, or an in-job retry recovered it), regression_test_count is owned tests that failed with no such proof and still hit min_failed_prs distinct PRs or master, and failed_run_count, same_commit_recovery_run_count and quarantined_failed_run_count count distinct CI runs across the team's owned tests, so one run with many failing tests counts once. Each has an equal-length previous-window twin (*_prior) for honest deltas. Use this for \"which team owns the flakiest surfaces right now\" and to route a flaky-test or CI Signal to its owning team. Ownership is stamped on the spans at CI emission time from the repo's ownership map (the distributed owners.yaml files); spans without a stamp aggregate under the literal team 'unowned' (a nonempty 'unowned' row means ownership gaps, not a real team), and a re-stamped test lands under its latest owner only. Each row also carries test_file_count (the daily owners.yaml census denominator, with a window-start twin) and merged_pr_count (merged PRs by the team's members, bots excluded); teams with census counts but no CI signal appear with zero signal counts and a null last_seen_at. Teams are organizational owners of code surfaces, never authors. Read all counts as absolute signal, never rates: fast passing runs are not emitted, so there is no honest denominator.",
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies the definition of the 'engineering-analytics-team-ci-health' tool description, changing the interpretation of failed_run_count and recovery counts from a potential rate or per-test count to a distinct CI run count. This could prevent downstream consumers from misinterpreting the metric, but the implementation and checks are not supplied.
